As an high-speed-internet-age kid (born in the 90s) I'm actually very curious to hear ones from older people who grew up before the internet, but it just happens that because of my age many of mine are internet-related:

-Either find a neighbor with unprotected wifi or get the neighbors' wifi password (this was easy for me as I was often the person who helped the neighbors' with their computer issues). Then you have 24/365 access to restriction-free internet no matter what your parents do on their router. Probably my favorite trick.

-If all they did was change the wifi password, I would just hit the "WPS" button (you press the button and it gives your computer the password, almost all home routers have one) to avoid having to please them in some way to get the password

-My dad would apply restrictions based on my PC's mac address. Spoofing my mac was pretty easy using free software or tools built into some Linux OS (just change the "cloned mac" in Linux Mint, I'd just take my real mac and change one number in it personally). Free tools for Windows are out there for Windows as well e.g.: https://technitium.com/tmac/

-If your parents try to take something away, hide it and pretend you "lost" it. Also having extra devices/chargers/game controllers your parents don't know about helps.

-using proxy sites or game clients rather than going directly to the online game's main site is an easy and free way to evade blocking

-I've found most web filters can't touch anything that uses https (as sites increasingly do by default or at the very least as an option these days)

So if your kids are as tech savvy and determined as I was, they have unconditional unrestricted 24/365 internet access and there's not really anything you can do about it.
